schedule.name: CDC child schedule
schedule.description: CDC 2025 edition, age-based, birth through 18. This is the edition before CDC's January 2026 revision. Conditions that add vaccines are separate risk schedules.
schedule.source: CDC Recommended Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule for Ages 18 Years or Younger, United States, 2025 (https://www.cdc.gov/vaccines/hcp/imz-schedules/child-adolescent-age.html)

rules.review_reason: RSV antibody depends on the RSV season and whether the pregnant parent had the RSV vaccine at least 14 days before delivery. Confirm.
rules.why_text: CDC child schedule 2025: infants under 8 months entering their first RSV season: 1 dose nirsevimab, depending on maternal RSV vaccination.

rules.review_reason: Age 8 to 19 months: 1 dose nirsevimab before the second RSV season only if at high risk of severe RSV disease. Confirm.
rules.why_text: CDC child schedule 2025: high-risk children entering a second RSV season.
CDC child schedule 2025: 3 doses at birth, 1 to 2 months and 6 to 18 months. The final dose is not given before 24 weeks of age.
CDC child schedule 2025: 2 doses at 2 and 4 months (Rotarix). RotaTeq needs a third dose at 6 months. Do not start on or after 15 weeks.

rules.review_reason: Rotavirus: Rotarix is complete after 2 doses; RotaTeq needs a third dose by 8 months. Check the product given. The series cannot be started now.
rules.why_text: CDC child schedule 2025: RotaTeq 3rd dose at 6 months; the final dose must be given by 8 months.
CDC child schedule 2025: 5 doses at 2, 4, 6, 15 to 18 months and 4 to 6 years. Dose 5 is not needed if dose 4 was given at age 4 or older.
CDC child schedule 2025: doses at 2, 4 and 6 months (PedvaxHIB is 2 primary doses).

rules.review_reason: Hib: PedvaxHIB is 3 doses in total, other products are 4. Check the product given, and follow the catch-up table if behind.
rules.why_text: CDC child schedule 2025: booster at 12 to 15 months.
CDC child schedule 2025: 4 doses at 2, 4, 6 and 12 to 15 months.
CDC child schedule 2025: 4 doses at 2, 4, 6 to 18 months and 4 to 6 years; the last dose is at age 4 or older and 6 months after the previous.

rules.review_reason: COVID-19 for ages 6 months to 17 years: shared clinical decision-making (not routine). Dosing depends on earlier doses and product; immunocompromised children have separate dosing. Confirm.
rules.why_text: CDC child schedule 2025: ages 6 months through 17 years, shared clinical decision-making.

rules.review_reason: Influenza at age 6 months to 8 years: 2 doses at least 4 weeks apart if fewer than 2 flu doses before July 1 of the previous season, otherwise 1 dose. Check history.
rules.why_text: CDC child schedule 2025: yearly from 6 months of age.
CDC child schedule 2025: age 9 or older, 1 dose every year.
CDC child schedule 2025: 2 doses at 12 to 15 months and 4 to 6 years.
CDC child schedule 2025: 2 doses at 12 to 15 months and 4 to 6 years (3 months apart at least; 4 weeks at age 13 or older).
CDC child schedule 2025: 2 doses at least 6 months apart, starting at 12 to 23 months. Catch-up through 18 years.
CDC child schedule 2025: age 11 to 12: 1 dose Tdap. Catch-up: 1 dose Tdap at 13 to 18 if never given.
CDC child schedule 2025: routine at 11 to 12 years (can start at 9): 2 doses 6 to 12 months apart (minimum 5 months). 3 doses if immunocompromised.

rules.review_reason: HPV: 3 doses if started at 15 or older; 2 doses if started at 9 to 14. Check earlier doses.
rules.why_text: CDC child schedule 2025: catch-up for everyone through age 18.
CDC child schedule 2025: dose 1 at 11 to 12 years, dose 2 at 16 years. At 13 to 15 with no dose: give 1 now and a booster at 16 to 18 (8 weeks apart at least).

rules.review_reason: MenACWY at 16 to 18: 1 dose if never vaccinated; a booster at 16 or older if the first dose was before 16. Check history.
rules.why_text: CDC child schedule 2025: 2 doses, the second at 16 years.

rules.review_reason: MenB at 16 to 18 (up to 23): shared clinical decision-making when not at increased risk.
rules.why_text: CDC child schedule 2025: age 16 to 23 (16 to 18 preferred), shared clinical decision-making.
